This document establishes the foundational framework governing retail banking relationships at Aurelia Bank. It defines the customer segmentation model, account categories, and general service principles that all product-specific manuals and operational policies build upon. Every retail-facing policy issued by Aurelia Bank, including the Home Loan Product Manual (AUR-HL-002), the Personal Loan Product Manual (AUR-PL-003), and the Digital Banking and Transaction Policy (AUR-DB-010), assumes the customer categories and terminology defined here.

The policy exists to ensure that branch staff, relationship managers, and operations teams apply a single, consistent definition of who a retail customer is, how that customer is classified, and what baseline entitlements and obligations attach to each classification. Without this shared foundation, product teams would apply inconsistent eligibility rules, and downstream compliance and risk policies would be unable to reference a stable customer taxonomy.

This policy applies to all Aurelia Bank retail branches, digital banking channels, relationship management staff, and branch operations personnel. It covers individual customers, small business customers, and the point at which a business customer graduates out of retail coverage into the corporate banking segment governed by the Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004). It does not govern institutional treasury clients or interbank counterparties, which fall outside the retail banking mandate entirely.

The policy applies from the moment a prospective customer initiates contact with Aurelia Bank through account opening, ongoing relationship management, and periodic review, up to and including account closure or reclassification.

Standard Retail Customer (SRC):: An individual customer whose average quarterly relationship balance is below AUR 1,000,000 and whose total relationship value is below AUR 5,000,000.

Aurelia Preferred Customer (APC):: An individual customer maintaining an average quarterly balance of AUR 1,000,000 or more, or a total relationship value of AUR 5,000,000 or more, across deposits, loans, and investment holdings.

Small Business Customer (SBC):: A sole proprietorship, partnership, or registered micro-enterprise with annual turnover below AUR 50,000,000, banking primarily through retail channels.

Corporate Customer (CC):: A registered company or business entity with annual turnover of AUR 250,000,000 or more, or any entity that has been formally reclassified out of the SBC segment. Corporate Customers are governed by the Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004) rather than this document.

Non-Resident Customer (NRC):: A customer whose primary residence and mailing address are outside Aurelia's domestic jurisdiction, subject to the enhanced verification requirements in the KYC and AML Policy (AUR-KYC-006).

Relationship Value (RV):: The aggregate value of a customer's deposits, outstanding loan balances, and investment holdings with Aurelia Bank, calculated monthly for segmentation purposes.

Aurelia Currency Unit (AUR):: The fictional functional currency used throughout Aurelia Bank's internal documentation and this synthetic corpus.

Aurelia Bank segments retail customers into four primary categories: Standard Retail Customer, Aurelia Preferred Customer, Small Business Customer, and Non-Resident Customer. Segmentation is recalculated on the first business day of each calendar quarter based on the preceding quarter's average balances and relationship value. A Standard Retail Customer whose average quarterly balance rises to AUR 1,000,000 or above is automatically reclassified as an Aurelia Preferred Customer at the next quarterly review, and gains access to preferred servicing queues, reduced fee schedules under the Interest Rate and Fee Policy (AUR-IRF-007), and a dedicated relationship manager.

A Small Business Customer whose annual turnover, as evidenced in the most recent audited or self-certified financial statement, exceeds AUR 50,000,000 in two consecutive financial years is flagged for graduation review. Once turnover exceeds AUR 250,000,000, the customer is formally reclassified as a Corporate Customer and transitioned to the Corporate Loan Policy framework; all retail-segment credit facilities are migrated or renegotiated under corporate terms within 180 calendar days of reclassification.

The retail product suite consists of the Aurelia Savings Access Account, the Aurelia Preferred Current Account, and the Aurelia Current Business Account. The Aurelia Savings Access Account requires a minimum average monthly balance of AUR 5,000 for Standard Retail Customers; falling below this threshold in a given month triggers a non-maintenance charge as specified in the Interest Rate and Fee Policy. Aurelia Preferred Customers opening a Preferred Current Account are required to maintain a minimum average monthly balance of AUR 50,000, in exchange for which the non-maintenance charge is waived and the customer receives priority processing on all loan applications under the Home Loan Product Manual and Personal Loan Product Manual.

The Aurelia Current Business Account is available exclusively to Small Business Customers and requires supporting business registration documentation as specified in the Customer Onboarding Policy (AUR-CO-005).

Any individual aged 18 years or older, who is legally competent to contract, is eligible to open a retail account in their own name. Minors between the ages of 10 and 18 may open a Minor Savings Account, operated jointly with a parent or legal guardian who has completed the standard onboarding process. Below the age of 10, an account may only be opened and operated entirely by the guardian on the minor's behalf.

Small Business Customers must be registered under an applicable business registration scheme and must present the registration certificate, proprietor or partner identification, and a business address proof at the time of account opening, consistent with the requirements of the Customer Onboarding Policy.

All retail account openings require completion of the standard Customer Due Diligence process defined in the KYC and AML Policy, including submission of a valid Proof of Identity, Proof of Address, and a recent photograph. Non-Resident Customers must additionally submit an overseas address proof and are subject to Enhanced Due Diligence prior to account activation.

Existing customers seeking reclassification from Standard Retail Customer to Aurelia Preferred Customer status ahead of the standard quarterly review may submit a Relationship Value Certification Request to their branch, supported by statements evidencing the qualifying balance or relationship value, for manual review by the Branch Manager.

Standard Retail Customers are subject to a daily cash deposit limit of AUR 500,000 per account without additional declaration, and a daily ATM cash withdrawal limit of AUR 50,000. Aurelia Preferred Customers receive an elevated ATM withdrawal limit of AUR 100,000 per day. Cash transactions of AUR 1,000,000 or more in a single day trigger mandatory reporting obligations under the KYC and AML Policy, regardless of customer category.

The minimum opening deposit for a Aurelia Savings Access Account is AUR 1,000. The minimum opening deposit for a Preferred Current Account is AUR 25,000.

Full-time students under the age of 25 who provide valid institutional enrollment proof are exempt from the minimum average balance requirement on the Aurelia Savings Access Account for the duration of their enrollment, subject to annual re-verification. Senior citizens aged 60 years or older receive a permanent waiver of the non-maintenance charge on Standard Savings accounts. Customers with certified disabilities affecting their ability to visit a branch in person may complete onboarding through the assisted digital onboarding channel described in the Digital Banking and Transaction Policy, subject to Branch Manager sign-off in place of an in-branch signature.

Account opening begins with prospective customer identification at the branch or through the digital onboarding channel, followed by document collection and verification as defined in the Customer Onboarding Policy. Upon successful KYC verification, the account is provisionally opened with restricted transaction limits for the first 5 business days, pending final compliance sign-off. Full transaction privileges are activated automatically on the sixth business day unless compliance flags the file for Enhanced Due Diligence, in which case activation is held pending resolution.

Quarterly segmentation reviews are run automatically by the retail systems team on the first business day of January, April, July, and October. Customers moving between categories are notified in writing within 10 business days of reclassification.

Account opening for Standard Retail Customers requires sign-off from a Branch Officer. Aurelia Preferred Customer account opening and any exception granted under this policy requires Branch Manager approval. Non-Resident Customer accounts require additional sign-off from the branch's designated Compliance Liaison prior to activation, in line with the KYC and AML Policy.

This version of the Retail Banking Policy, Version 3.2, is effective from 1 January 2026 and supersedes Version 3.1, dated 1 July 2024. All branches were required to complete staff briefings on the revised segmentation thresholds by 15 January 2026.

This policy defines the four retail customer categories used across all Aurelia Bank documentation: Standard Retail Customer, Aurelia Preferred Customer, Small Business Customer, and Non-Resident Customer, along with the numerical thresholds that govern segmentation, reclassification into the corporate segment, account minimums, and transaction limits. It serves as the reference point for eligibility and terminology used throughout the Home Loan, Personal Loan, Onboarding, KYC/AML, Interest Rate and Fee, and Digital Banking policies.

This manual sets out the product specifications, eligibility criteria, and operating procedures for Aurelia Home Advantage, Aurelia Bank's secured home loan product. It is intended for use by branch lending staff, credit analysts, and loan processing operations to originate, assess, and disburse home loans consistently across all branches. It should be read together with the Retail Banking Policy (AUR-RB-001), which defines the customer categories referenced here, and the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy (AUR-CR-008), which defines the risk grading applied to every applicant.

This manual applies to all home loan applications originated by Standard Retail Customers and Aurelia Preferred Customers for the purchase, construction, or extension of residential property, and for the refinancing of existing home loans held with other institutions. It does not apply to commercial real estate lending, which falls under the Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004), nor to unsecured borrowing, which is addressed in the Personal Loan Product Manual (AUR-PL-003).

Aurelia Home Advantage:: The branded home loan product offered under this manual, available in Fixed Rate and Floating Rate variants.

Loan-to-Value Ratio (LTV):: The ratio of the sanctioned loan amount to the assessed market value of the mortgaged property, expressed as a percentage.

Aurelia Base Lending Rate (ABLR):: The reference interest rate published quarterly by Aurelia Bank's Treasury division, against which floating-rate home loan pricing is benchmarked. ABLR is currently 8.75% per annum as of the effective date of this manual.

Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI):: The ratio of an applicant's total monthly debt obligations, including the proposed home loan installment, to their verified monthly income.

Aurelia Credit Score (ACS):: The proprietary credit score, ranging from 300 to 900, assigned to each applicant under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy, which determines the applicant's Risk Grade and applicable interest rate spread.

Applicants must be Standard Retail Customers or Aurelia Preferred Customers as defined in the Retail Banking Policy, aged at least 21 years at the time of application. Salaried applicants must not exceed age 65 at loan maturity; self-employed applicants must not exceed age 65 at loan maturity under standard terms, though an exception to age 70 is available under the conditions described below. Applicants must have a minimum Aurelia Credit Score of 650, corresponding to Risk Grade C or better under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy; applicants below this threshold are not eligible for Aurelia Home Advantage under standard underwriting.

Co-applicants are permitted, and a co-applicant's income may be combined with the primary applicant's income for the purpose of loan amount and DTI calculation, provided the co-applicant is a spouse, parent, or sibling of the primary applicant and is a party to the property title.

Salaried applicants must provide the most recent 3 months of salary statements, the most recent 2 years of income tax filings, and an employment continuity letter. Self-employed applicants must provide 2 years of audited or self-certified financial statements and 2 years of income tax filings, consistent with the documentation standards described in the Customer Onboarding Policy (AUR-CO-005).

All applicants must provide a registered sale agreement or construction agreement for the property being financed, and the property must undergo a valuation by an Aurelia Bank-empanelled valuer prior to sanction. Property title must be verified as free of encumbrance by the bank's legal team before disbursement.

Aurelia Home Advantage loans range from a minimum of AUR 500,000 to a maximum of AUR 25,000,000. The maximum Loan-to-Value Ratio is 80% of assessed property value for salaried applicants and 75% for self-employed applicants. Maximum loan tenure is 30 years, subject to the applicant's age at maturity not exceeding the limits described in Eligibility. The maximum permissible Debt-to-Income Ratio, inclusive of the proposed home loan installment and all existing obligations, is 45%.

Interest rates on the Floating Rate variant are priced at ABLR plus a spread determined by Risk Grade: Risk Grade A applicants receive a spread of 0.40%, Risk Grade B a spread of 0.85%, and Risk Grade C a spread of 1.85%, all as defined under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy and the Interest Rate and Fee Policy (AUR-IRF-007). The processing fee is 0.50% of the sanctioned loan amount, subject to a minimum of AUR 5,000 and a maximum of AUR 75,000, as detailed in the Interest Rate and Fee Policy.

Every Aurelia Home Advantage loan requires the mortgaged property to be covered by a fire and structural insurance policy for the full outstanding loan amount throughout the loan tenure, with Aurelia Bank named as the loss payee. Borrowers are additionally offered, though not mandated to purchase, an Aurelia Loan Protection Cover, a reducing-balance term insurance product that settles the outstanding loan balance in the event of the borrower's death, with a one-time premium that may be financed within the loan amount subject to the maximum LTV limits described below. Property insurance lapses of more than 15 calendar days trigger an automated notice to the borrower and, if unresolved within 30 calendar days, Aurelia Bank may arrange a force-placed policy at the borrower's cost.

Borrowers on the Floating Rate variant may make part-payments of any amount, subject to a minimum of AUR 25,000 per part-payment, without restriction on frequency, and without any part-payment charge, consistent with the foreclosure treatment described in the Interest Rate and Fee Policy. Borrowers on the Fixed Rate variant may make part-payments up to a cumulative maximum of 25% of the original principal per calendar year without charge; part-payments beyond this threshold attract the same foreclosure charge schedule applicable to full foreclosure. Every part-payment is applied to principal, and the borrower may elect to either reduce the monthly installment or shorten the remaining tenure, with tenure reduction applied by default absent an explicit borrower instruction.

Self-employed applicants with a Risk Grade A rating and a minimum of 5 years of continuous business operating history may be extended the loan tenure such that maturity age reaches 70 years, provided the loan is additionally secured by a fixed deposit lien of no less than 20% of the sanctioned amount, approved by the Regional Credit Committee. Applicants with an Aurelia Credit Score between 600 and 649, ordinarily Risk Grade D and therefore ineligible, may be considered on an exception basis if the LTV is capped at 60% and a co-applicant with a minimum Aurelia Credit Score of 750 is added to the application, subject to Central Credit Committee approval.

Upon receipt of a complete application, the branch lending officer performs an initial document check within 2 business days. The file is then forwarded to the credit analysis team, which completes income verification, DTI calculation, and Aurelia Credit Score retrieval within a further 3 business days. Property valuation and legal title verification are conducted in parallel and are expected to conclude within 7 business days of application. Upon receipt of a satisfactory valuation and legal report, the file is routed to the appropriate approval authority based on the sanctioned amount. Disbursement occurs within 3 business days of final approval and execution of loan documentation, either as a single disbursement for ready property purchase or in construction-linked tranches for under-construction property, with each tranche tied to a verified stage of construction.

Sanction letters issued to approved applicants remain valid for 90 calendar days from the date of issue; if disbursement has not occurred within this window, the applicant must undergo a re-verification of income and Aurelia Credit Score before disbursement can proceed. For construction-linked disbursements, a moratorium period of up to 24 months from first disbursement is available during which only interest is payable on the disbursed amount; full principal and interest installments commence either at the end of the moratorium period or upon full disbursement, whichever occurs first. Stamp duty, registration charges, and legal documentation fees associated with the mortgage are borne by the borrower and are not included in the sanctioned loan amount or in the LTV calculation.

The complete loan file, including the application, income documents, valuation report, legal opinion, and signed loan agreement, is retained in the bank's document management system for the full loan tenure plus an additional 8 years following final closure, consistent with the record retention standard set out in the Financial Compliance Regulation (AUR-FC-009). Any subsequent modification to loan terms, including part-payment tenure adjustments or rate reset elections, is logged as an addendum to the original loan agreement and retained under the same schedule.

Applications up to AUR 2,000,000 may be approved by the Branch Manager. Applications between AUR 2,000,000 and AUR 10,000,000 require Regional Credit Committee approval. Applications exceeding AUR 10,000,000, and all exception cases described above, require Central Credit Committee approval. Every sanctioned home loan is subject to an annual portfolio review by the Credit Risk team as described in the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy.

Version 2.4 of the Home Loan Product Manual is effective from 1 March 2026, superseding Version 2.3 dated 1 September 2024. The revised Risk Grade-based spread structure introduced in this version replaces the flat-spread model used prior to March 2026.

Aurelia Home Advantage offers secured home loans between AUR 500,000 and AUR 25,000,000, at up to 80% LTV for salaried applicants and 75% for self-employed applicants, over tenures of up to 30 years. Pricing is benchmarked to the Aurelia Base Lending Rate plus a Risk Grade-dependent spread, with a minimum Aurelia Credit Score of 650 required under standard underwriting and defined exception paths available for otherwise ineligible applicants under additional security and senior approval.

This manual defines the eligibility criteria, pricing structure, and processing workflow for Aurelia Personal Credit Line, Aurelia Bank's unsecured personal loan product. It is intended to guide branch lending staff and the centralized personal loan underwriting team in originating and disbursing personal loans in a manner consistent with the bank's credit risk framework.

This manual applies to all unsecured personal loan applications submitted by Standard Retail Customers and Aurelia Preferred Customers, as defined in the Retail Banking Policy (AUR-RB-001), for purposes including debt consolidation, medical expenses, travel, and other personal financing needs. It does not apply to secured lending products such as Aurelia Home Advantage, governed by the Home Loan Product Manual (AUR-HL-002), and it does not apply to business or corporate borrowing.

Aurelia Personal Credit Line:: The branded unsecured personal loan product offered under this manual.

Unsecured Facility:: A credit facility extended without collateral, relying solely on the applicant's income and Aurelia Credit Score for risk assessment.

Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI):: As defined in the Home Loan Product Manual, the ratio of total monthly debt obligations, including the proposed loan installment, to verified monthly income.

Aurelia Credit Score (ACS):: The proprietary credit score, ranging from 300 to 900, described in the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy (AUR-CR-008), used to determine an applicant's Risk Grade.

Applicants must be between 21 and 58 years of age at the time of application, and must not exceed 60 years of age at loan maturity, reflecting the shorter maximum tenure and unsecured nature of this product relative to Aurelia Home Advantage. Applicants must hold a Standard Retail Customer or Aurelia Preferred Customer account with Aurelia Bank for a minimum of 6 months, or must be salaried employees of a corporate entity on Aurelia Bank's approved employer list, in which case the minimum relationship period is waived.

A minimum Aurelia Credit Score of 600 is required, corresponding to Risk Grade D or better. Applicants with a Risk Grade of E, meaning an Aurelia Credit Score below 600, are not eligible for Aurelia Personal Credit Line under any circumstance, as the product carries no collateral to offset elevated default risk.

Salaried applicants must submit the most recent 3 months of salary statements and a current employment verification letter. Self-employed applicants must submit the most recent 1 year of audited or self-certified financial statements and the most recent year of income tax filings. All applicants must complete the standard Customer Due Diligence process described in the Customer Onboarding Policy (AUR-CO-005) if not already an existing verified customer.

Applicants with existing unsecured debt exceeding AUR 1,000,000 across all lenders, as reported through the applicant's credit bureau disclosure, must provide a written explanation of repayment capacity, which is reviewed manually by the credit analyst regardless of Aurelia Credit Score.

The stated purpose of the loan must be disclosed at application, selected from a defined list including debt consolidation, medical expense, travel, home renovation, education, and general personal use. Loans disclosed for debt consolidation require the applicant to provide statements for the facilities being consolidated, and Aurelia Bank reserves the right to disburse the consolidation amount directly to the identified lenders rather than to the applicant, at the discretion of the underwriting officer, in order to confirm the stated purpose is fulfilled.

The centralized unsecured lending unit is responsible for end-to-end processing of all Aurelia Personal Credit Line applications, regardless of the branch at which the customer initiated the request. Branch staff are responsible only for initial application capture and document collection where a customer applies in person; all underwriting, approval within delegated limits, and disbursement decisions rest with the centralized unit. The Collections and Recovery unit assumes responsibility for any account once it is classified as a Special Mention Account, as described below.

Aurelia Personal Credit Line loans range from a minimum of AUR 50,000 to a maximum of AUR 2,000,000. Loan tenure ranges from 12 to 60 months. The maximum permissible Debt-to-Income Ratio, inclusive of the proposed installment, is 50%, five percentage points higher than the equivalent limit for Aurelia Home Advantage, reflecting the shorter average tenure of personal loans.

Fixed interest rates range from 11.5% per annum for Risk Grade A applicants to 19.75% per annum for Risk Grade D applicants, as detailed in the Interest Rate and Fee Policy (AUR-IRF-007). The processing fee is 1.75% of the approved loan amount, subject to a minimum of AUR 1,000 and a maximum of AUR 25,000.

Approved loan amounts are disbursed as a single lump sum credit to the applicant's Aurelia Bank account; Aurelia Personal Credit Line does not support tranche-based or partial disbursement under any circumstance, distinguishing it from the construction-linked disbursement structure available under Aurelia Home Advantage. Repayment is structured as equal monthly installments over the selected tenure, with the first installment due 30 calendar days after disbursement. Borrowers may switch their scheduled installment date once per calendar year, subject to a minimum 5 business day advance request to the centralized unsecured lending unit.

Existing Aurelia Preferred Customers with a minimum relationship tenure of 3 years and a Risk Grade of A may be extended a processing fee waiver at the discretion of the Branch Manager. Applicants employed by an Aurelia Bank-approved employer with a Risk Grade of D, ordinarily capped at the standard maximum loan amount, may be considered for loans up to AUR 3,000,000 where the employer has a salary-assignment arrangement with Aurelia Bank, subject to Regional Credit Committee approval and an additional 1.5% rate loading over the standard Risk Grade D rate.

Personal loan applications are processed through the centralized unsecured lending unit rather than at branch level. Upon submission, the applicant's Aurelia Credit Score and existing credit bureau exposure are retrieved electronically within 1 business day. Income documents are verified within a further 1 business day for salaried applicants, or 2 business days for self-employed applicants. Approved applications are disbursed by direct credit to the applicant's Aurelia Bank account within 1 business day of final sign-off, making the standard end-to-end turnaround 2 to 4 business days depending on employment type.

Applications up to AUR 500,000 may be approved by the Branch Manager or, for applications submitted through the centralized unit, by the designated Personal Loan Underwriting Officer. Applications between AUR 500,000 and AUR 2,000,000 require Regional Credit Committee approval. All exception cases, including the elevated employer-linked limit described above, require Regional Credit Committee approval regardless of amount.

Version 1.8 of the Personal Loan Product Manual is effective from 15 January 2026, superseding Version 1.7 dated 1 June 2025. This version introduces the employer-linked exception limit and revises the maximum DTI from 48% to 50%.

The loan file, including the application, income verification documents, and signed loan agreement, is retained in the bank's document management system for the loan tenure plus 8 years following final closure, consistent with the retention standard defined in the Financial Compliance Regulation (AUR-FC-009). Because Aurelia Personal Credit Line is unsecured, no collateral or valuation records are generated or retained, distinguishing the file composition from that of Aurelia Home Advantage.

Accounts that fall between 30 and 89 days past due are classified as Special Mention Accounts under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy and are transferred to the centralized collections queue, which attempts contact through the registered mobile number and email on file. Accounts reaching 90 days past due are classified as Non-Performing Exposures, at which point the file is referred to the Recovery unit and the customer's Aurelia Credit Score reflects the default, materially reducing eligibility for any future Aurelia Bank credit product.

Aurelia Personal Credit Line differs from Aurelia Home Advantage in three structural respects that staff should keep in mind when advising customers who may qualify for either product. First, pricing is materially higher, reflecting the absence of collateral: even a Risk Grade A personal loan applicant, priced at 11.5% per annum, pays more than a Risk Grade C home loan applicant, priced at ABLR plus 1.85%. Second, processing is centralized and faster, with a standard turnaround of 2 to 4 business days against 10 to 15 business days for a typical home loan. Third, the maximum facility size of AUR 2,000,000 is a small fraction of the AUR 25,000,000 ceiling available under Aurelia Home Advantage, reflecting the higher risk concentration the bank is willing to accept without collateral.

Aurelia Personal Credit Line offers unsecured loans between AUR 50,000 and AUR 2,000,000, over tenures of 12 to 60 months, to applicants with a minimum Aurelia Credit Score of 600. Pricing ranges from 11.5% to 19.75% per annum by Risk Grade, with a processing fee of 1.75% of the approved amount and a maximum Debt-to-Income Ratio of 50%, reflecting a faster, centrally underwritten process distinct from the branch-led, collateral-backed Home Loan workflow.

This policy governs the origination, assessment, approval, and monitoring of credit facilities extended to Corporate Customers of Aurelia Bank. It defines the two principal corporate lending products, Aurelia Corporate Term Finance and the Aurelia Working Capital Facility, and establishes the underwriting standards, collateral requirements, and approval hierarchy applicable to corporate lending decisions.

This policy applies to all lending relationships with Corporate Customers, defined under the Retail Banking Policy (AUR-RB-001) as entities with annual turnover of AUR 250,000,000 or more, or entities formally reclassified from Small Business Customer status. It is used by the Corporate Banking division, Regional Corporate Credit Committees, and the Senior Credit Committee. It does not apply to retail lending products, which are governed separately by the Home Loan Product Manual (AUR-HL-002) and Personal Loan Product Manual (AUR-PL-003).

Aurelia Corporate Term Finance:: A fixed-tenure secured credit facility extended to Corporate Customers for capital expenditure, expansion, or asset acquisition purposes.

Aurelia Working Capital Facility:: A revolving, annually renewable credit facility extended against a Corporate Customer's current assets to fund operating cycle requirements.

Aurelia Corporate Reference Rate (ACRR):: The benchmark rate published quarterly by Aurelia Bank's Treasury division for corporate lending, currently 9.10% per annum as of the effective date of this policy.

Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR):: The ratio of a borrower's annual net operating income to its total annual debt service obligations, used to assess repayment capacity for term facilities.

Hypothecation:: A form of security interest under which movable assets such as inventory or receivables are pledged as collateral without transfer of physical possession to the lender.

A Corporate Customer must have been in continuous business operation for at least 3 years to be eligible for Aurelia Corporate Term Finance, and at least 2 years to be eligible for the Aurelia Working Capital Facility. The applicant entity must be classified as Risk Grade C or better under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy (AUR-CR-008), and must demonstrate a minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 1.25x for any proposed term facility, calculated on a trailing 12-month basis and projected over the facility tenure.

Entities operating in industries classified as Restricted Sectors under the Financial Compliance Regulation (AUR-FC-009) are not eligible for corporate lending under this policy regardless of financial standing, unless a specific exemption has been granted by the Board Credit Committee.

Every corporate applicant must provide audited financial statements for the preceding 3 financial years, prepared by a registered independent auditor. Applicants must additionally provide a board resolution authorizing the borrowing, a corporate structure chart identifying beneficial ownership as required under the KYC and AML Policy (AUR-KYC-006), and, for Working Capital Facility applicants, a minimum of 12 months of bank statements evidencing operating cash flows.

Term Finance applicants must submit a detailed project or capital expenditure plan, including projected cash flows for the facility tenure, and must provide collateral valuation reports from an Aurelia Bank-empanelled valuer.

Aurelia Corporate Term Finance is available from a minimum of AUR 5,000,000 to a maximum of AUR 500,000,000, with a maximum tenure of 10 years. The Aurelia Working Capital Facility is available up to a maximum limit of AUR 200,000,000, renewable annually subject to satisfactory account conduct and updated financial review.

Term Finance facilities must be secured to a minimum of 100% of the sanctioned amount by fixed assets, typically property, plant, or equipment. Working Capital Facilities are secured by hypothecation of inventory and receivables, subject to a maximum drawing margin of 75% of the hypothecated asset value, meaning the borrower may draw up to 75% of the value of eligible inventory and receivables at any time.

Pricing for both products is benchmarked to the Aurelia Corporate Reference Rate plus a spread determined by Risk Grade: 0.75% for Risk Grade A, 1.50% for Risk Grade B, and 2.75% for Risk Grade C, as further detailed in the Interest Rate and Fee Policy (AUR-IRF-007). The processing fee is 1.00% of the sanctioned limit, subject to a cap of AUR 2,000,000; for facilities above AUR 50,000,000, the processing fee is negotiable subject to Senior Credit Committee approval.

Every Aurelia Corporate Term Finance facility carries a standard set of financial covenants tested quarterly, including maintenance of the minimum 1.25x DSCR, a maximum total-debt-to-equity ratio of 2.5x, and a minimum current ratio of 1.1x. A covenant breach does not automatically trigger default but requires the borrower to submit a remediation plan to the Corporate Banking Relationship Manager within 15 business days; two consecutive quarterly breaches of the same covenant escalate the facility to the Corporate Watchlist for enhanced monitoring, including monthly rather than quarterly financial reporting from the borrower.

Working Capital Facilities are subject to a monthly drawing power certificate, in which the borrower reports current inventory and receivables levels, against which the 75% drawing margin is recalculated. A drawing power shortfall, where outstanding utilization exceeds the recalculated available margin, must be regularized by the borrower within 7 business days through either repayment or additional eligible collateral.

A Corporate Customer with fewer than 3 years of operating history may be considered for Aurelia Corporate Term Finance if the facility is fully secured by a fixed deposit lien or bank guarantee covering 100% of the sanctioned amount, subject to Senior Credit Committee approval. A DSCR below 1.25x, down to a floor of 1.10x, may be accepted where the borrower's parent entity provides an unconditional corporate guarantee rated Risk Grade A or better, subject to Board Credit Committee approval.

Corporate loan applications are managed by a dedicated Relationship Manager within the Corporate Banking division, who coordinates document collection and initial screening within 5 business days. The application is then referred to the Corporate Credit Analysis team for financial spreading, DSCR calculation, and Risk Grade assignment, a process expected to take 7 to 10 business days depending on facility complexity. Collateral valuation and legal due diligence proceed in parallel. Upon completion, the file is routed to the appropriate approval authority based on facility size. Disbursement for Term Finance facilities may occur in a single tranche or in project-linked tranches; Working Capital Facilities are activated as an available limit rather than disbursed as a lump sum.

Facilities up to AUR 50,000,000 require Regional Corporate Credit Committee approval. Facilities between AUR 50,000,000 and AUR 200,000,000 require Senior Credit Committee approval. Facilities exceeding AUR 200,000,000, and all exception cases described above, require Board Credit Committee approval. All corporate facilities are subject to an annual credit review, and Working Capital Facilities require full renewal underwriting each year prior to the annual review date.

This policy defines the document requirements, verification steps, and turnaround standards for onboarding new customers at Aurelia Bank, across both retail and corporate segments. It operationalizes the Customer Due Diligence requirements set out in the KYC and AML Policy (AUR-KYC-006) into a concrete document checklist and processing workflow for branch and digital onboarding staff. Consistent onboarding practice matters not only for customer experience but for regulatory defensibility: every account Aurelia Bank opens must be traceable back to a documented, policy-compliant verification event, and this policy is the single reference staff use to demonstrate that traceability during an internal audit or an AFRC examination.

This policy applies to the onboarding of all new customers, including Standard Retail Customers, Aurelia Preferred Customers, Small Business Customers, Non-Resident Customers, and Corporate Customers, as categorized in the Retail Banking Policy (AUR-RB-001). It covers onboarding through branch channels, the assisted digital onboarding channel, and the fully digital self-service channel described in the Digital Banking and Transaction Policy (AUR-DB-010).

Proof of Identity (POI):: A government-issued document establishing a customer's identity, such as a national identity card or passport.

Proof of Address (POA):: A document establishing a customer's current residential or business address.

Aurelia Tax Identification Number (ATIN):: The unique tax identifier required for all customers opening an account with Aurelia Bank, used for regulatory reporting under the Financial Compliance Regulation (AUR-FC-009).

Customer Due Diligence (CDD):: The standard identity and address verification process applied to all new customers, as defined in the KYC and AML Policy.

Turnaround Time (TAT):: The elapsed business time between application submission and account activation.

Any individual meeting the age requirements of the Retail Banking Policy, and any business entity holding valid registration documentation, is eligible to be onboarded, subject to successful completion of Customer Due Diligence. Applicants who have previously been offboarded from Aurelia Bank due to a confirmed compliance violation are not eligible for re-onboarding without prior written clearance from the Compliance division.

Individual retail applicants must submit one valid Proof of Identity, one valid Proof of Address, a recent passport-sized photograph, and their Aurelia Tax Identification Number. Acceptable forms of Proof of Identity include a national identity card, a passport, or a driving license bearing a photograph; a bank-issued document is never accepted as a standalone Proof of Identity, as it does not constitute independent third-party verification. A Proof of Address in the form of a utility bill must be dated within the preceding 3 months; a government-issued address document is accepted if issued within the preceding 2 years. Where a submitted POI and POA do not match in name due to a legal name change, a supporting name-change certificate is required.

Small Business Customers must additionally provide a business registration certificate, proprietor or partner identification for all named principals, and a business address proof. Corporate Customers must provide the documentation set out in the Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004), including a board resolution, certificate of incorporation, and beneficial ownership declaration, as required under the KYC and AML Policy.

Non-Resident Customers must provide an overseas address proof in addition to the standard POI and POA, and are subject to the Enhanced Due Diligence procedure described in the KYC and AML Policy prior to account activation.

Standard retail onboarding through the branch channel carries a target Turnaround Time of 2 business days from complete document submission to account activation. This 2 business day target is measured from the point of complete document submission, not from initial applicant contact, and excludes any period spent by the applicant gathering outstanding documents under the incomplete-application process described below. Corporate onboarding carries a target Turnaround Time of 5 business days, reflecting the additional beneficial ownership and Enhanced Due Diligence verification required. Digital self-service onboarding for Standard Retail Customers carries a target Turnaround Time of 1 business day where identity can be verified electronically against the national identity database.

Newly onboarded accounts are subject to a provisional transaction limit of AUR 50,000 per day for the first 5 business days following account opening, as referenced in the Retail Banking Policy, pending final compliance sign-off.

Customers onboarding through the assisted digital channel due to a certified disability, as recognized under the Retail Banking Policy, may complete identity verification through a video-based verification call with a designated onboarding officer in place of in-person document presentation, provided the call is recorded and retained per the record-retention standards in the Financial Compliance Regulation. Small Business Customers unable to provide a formal business registration certificate because their jurisdiction of operation does not issue one may be onboarded on the basis of a notarized declaration of business activity, subject to Branch Manager approval and a reduced initial transaction limit of AUR 25,000 per day for the first 30 calendar days.

Onboarding begins with document collection at the branch, through the assisted digital channel, or through the digital self-service application. Collected documents are logged into the onboarding system and routed to the verification queue. A Verification Officer checks document authenticity and completeness, and cross-references the applicant against the Financial Intelligence Unit-Aurelia watchlist as required under the KYC and AML Policy. Upon successful verification, the account is provisionally activated with restricted limits as described above. A final compliance review is conducted within the first 5 business days, following which full transaction privileges are unlocked automatically unless the file has been escalated for Enhanced Due Diligence, in which case the provisional limits remain in place until resolution.

The Verification Officer is responsible for first-line document authenticity checks and watchlist screening at the point of onboarding. The Branch Manager is responsible for approving any exception case and for periodic review of onboarding volumes and rejection rates at the branch level. The Compliance Liaison, a role designated at each branch, is responsible for the additional sign-off required for Corporate and Non-Resident Customer onboarding, and serves as the branch's point of escalation for any onboarding file requiring Enhanced Due Diligence under the KYC and AML Policy.

An onboarding application is marked incomplete, rather than rejected, if required documents are missing, and the applicant is given 15 calendar days to submit the outstanding items before the application is automatically closed. An application is marked rejected where submitted documents fail authenticity verification, where the applicant appears on the Financial Intelligence Unit-Aurelia watchlist, or where the applicant has been previously offboarded for a confirmed compliance violation without subsequent Compliance clearance. Rejected applications are retained in the onboarding system for 2 years for audit purposes, and the applicant is not automatically notified of the specific reason for rejection where doing so would conflict with the confidentiality provisions of the KYC and AML Policy.

Standard individual onboarding may be approved by a Verification Officer upon successful document and watchlist checks. Onboarding involving any exception described above requires Branch Manager approval. Corporate and Non-Resident Customer onboarding requires additional sign-off from the branch's designated Compliance Liaison prior to final activation.

This policy establishes Aurelia Bank's Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering framework, including customer risk rating, Enhanced Due Diligence triggers, transaction monitoring thresholds, and suspicious activity reporting obligations. It provides the compliance foundation referenced by the Customer Onboarding Policy (AUR-CO-005) and applies to every customer relationship maintained by Aurelia Bank. This policy exists because Aurelia Bank's exposure to money-laundering and terrorist-financing risk is managed primarily through consistent, well-documented customer classification and monitoring rather than through any single control; staff across onboarding, transaction monitoring, and compliance investigation all draw their authority and their obligations from this document.

This policy applies to all customer categories defined in the Retail Banking Policy (AUR-RB-001), all onboarding channels described in the Customer Onboarding Policy, and all transaction monitoring activity across branch, digital, and corporate banking channels. It governs the conduct of all Aurelia Bank staff involved in customer verification, transaction monitoring, and regulatory reporting, and is issued under the authority of the Financial Compliance Regulation (AUR-FC-009).

Customer Due Diligence (CDD):: The standard process of verifying customer identity and address, and assessing the purpose and nature of the customer relationship, applied to every new customer.

Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD):: An intensified verification process applied to customers or transactions presenting elevated money-laundering or terrorist-financing risk, involving additional documentation, senior sign-off, and more frequent ongoing monitoring.

Politically Exposed Person (PEP):: An individual who holds, or has held within the preceding 5 years, a prominent public function, including their immediate family members and close associates, as defined for the purposes of this policy.

Suspicious Transaction Report (STR):: A formal report filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit-Aurelia (FIU-A) when a transaction or pattern of transactions is reasonably suspected of being linked to money laundering or other financial crime.

Cash Transaction Report (CTR):: A formal report filed with FIU-A for any single-day cash transaction, or series of connected cash transactions, meeting or exceeding the reporting threshold defined in this policy.

Financial Intelligence Unit-Aurelia (FIU-A):: The fictional national body to which Aurelia Bank reports suspicious and high-value cash transactions under this synthetic regulatory framework.

All customers, without exception, must complete Customer Due Diligence before an account is activated for unrestricted use, as described in the Customer Onboarding Policy. Customers classified as Politically Exposed Persons, customers operating cash-intensive businesses such as retail trading or hospitality, Non-Resident Customers, and any customer conducting a single cash transaction of AUR 1,000,000 or more are automatically routed into the Enhanced Due Diligence pathway regardless of their retail segment classification.

Standard Customer Due Diligence requires verification of a Proof of Identity and Proof of Address as described in the Customer Onboarding Policy, together with a declaration of the purpose of the account relationship. Enhanced Due Diligence additionally requires a declared source of funds statement, verification of the customer's occupation or business activity against the declared income level, and, for corporate applicants, identification of all beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the entity's shares or voting rights.

Every customer is assigned a KYC Risk Rating of Low, Medium, or High at onboarding, based on factors including customer category, geography, product usage, and PEP status. The KYC Risk Rating determines the frequency of periodic re-verification: Low Risk customers are re-verified every 8 years, Medium Risk customers every 3 years, and High Risk customers, including all PEPs, every 1 year.

Any single-day cash transaction, or aggregated same-day cash transactions, totaling AUR 1,000,000 or more triggers mandatory Cash Transaction Report filing with FIU-A, regardless of customer category or KYC Risk Rating. Suspicious Transaction Reports must be filed with FIU-A within 7 business days of an employee or automated monitoring system forming a reasonable suspicion, irrespective of the transaction amount involved.

Corporate beneficial ownership declarations are required for any individual or entity holding 25% or more of shares, voting rights, or equivalent ownership interest. Transaction monitoring systems flag any account showing a month-on-month transaction volume increase of 300% or more for manual review, even where no individual transaction breaches the CTR threshold.

Government and quasi-government entities are exempt from beneficial ownership declaration requirements, as their ownership structure is a matter of public record. Existing Low Risk customers who are re-verified ahead of schedule due to a product upgrade, such as reclassification to Aurelia Preferred Customer status, are not required to complete a full EDD cycle solely due to the reclassification, provided no other EDD trigger is present.

Transaction monitoring is performed continuously by an automated system that screens all transactions against the cash thresholds, watchlist matches, and behavioral pattern rules described in this policy. Flagged transactions are queued for review by a Compliance Analyst within 2 business days. Where the analyst confirms reasonable suspicion, an STR is drafted and submitted to FIU-A within the 7 business day filing window described above. CTR filings are generated automatically by the monitoring system and submitted to FIU-A on a next-business-day basis following the qualifying transaction.

Periodic re-verification is triggered automatically by the KYC system based on each customer's assigned risk rating and the date of their last verification. Customers due for re-verification are contacted at least 30 calendar days before their existing verification lapses; failure to complete re-verification within 60 calendar days of the due date results in the account being placed into restricted mode, permitting withdrawals but not new deposits, until re-verification is complete.

The Compliance Analyst is responsible for first-line review of system-flagged transactions and for drafting STR filings where suspicion is confirmed. The Senior Compliance Analyst is responsible for countersigning every STR prior to submission and for periodic quality review of closed monitoring cases. The Head of Compliance is responsible for approving all PEP relationships and for the bank's overall AML program, including annual reporting to the Board on the effectiveness of the transaction monitoring system.

In addition to the Financial Intelligence Unit-Aurelia watchlist, every customer and every counterparty named in a transaction is screened against Aurelia Bank's consolidated sanctions list at onboarding and on a daily basis thereafter for the life of the relationship. A positive sanctions match results in the immediate freezing of the account pending manual review by the Head of Compliance, and no transaction may be processed on a frozen account, including withdrawals, until the match is either confirmed as a genuine hit and escalated to FIU-A, or cleared as a false positive.

Standard CDD approval rests with the Verification Officer completing onboarding. EDD cases require sign-off from the branch's designated Compliance Liaison, and PEP relationships additionally require approval from the Head of Compliance before account activation. All STR filings must be reviewed and countersigned by a Senior Compliance Analyst prior to submission to FIU-A.

This policy consolidates the interest rate benchmarks, pricing spreads, and fee schedules applied across Aurelia Bank's deposit and lending products. It is the authoritative reference for all rate and fee figures cited in the Home Loan Product Manual (AUR-HL-002), Personal Loan Product Manual (AUR-PL-003), Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004), and Retail Banking Policy (AUR-RB-001); where any other document states a figure, this policy governs in the event of a discrepancy pending formal reconciliation.

This policy applies to all interest-bearing deposit accounts, all lending products, and all transaction and service fees charged by Aurelia Bank to retail, small business, and corporate customers. It is maintained jointly by the Treasury division, which sets benchmark rates, and the Product division, which sets fee schedules.

Aurelia Base Lending Rate (ABLR):: The benchmark rate for retail lending, reviewed and published quarterly by Treasury, currently 8.75% per annum.

Aurelia Corporate Reference Rate (ACRR):: The benchmark rate for corporate lending, reviewed and published quarterly by Treasury, currently 9.10% per annum.

Spread:: The percentage added to the applicable benchmark rate to arrive at a customer's final interest rate, determined by product and Risk Grade.

Foreclosure Charge:: A fee applied when a borrower repays a loan in full ahead of its scheduled tenure.

Non-Maintenance Charge:: A fee applied to a deposit account when the average balance falls below the minimum required for that account type.

All active loan and deposit accounts are subject to this policy. Rate and fee applicability depends on the Risk Grade assigned under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy (AUR-CR-008) and the customer category assigned under the Retail Banking Policy.

Benchmark rates are reviewed by Treasury at the start of each calendar quarter and published to all branches and digital channels no later than the second business day of the quarter. Any change to ABLR or ACRR is applied to new originations immediately and to existing floating-rate accounts on their next scheduled reset date, which occurs quarterly in alignment with the loan's disbursement anniversary.

Home loan floating rates are priced at ABLR plus a Risk Grade spread of 0.40% for Grade A, 0.85% for Grade B, and 1.85% for Grade C, as detailed in the Home Loan Product Manual. Personal loan fixed rates range from 11.5% per annum for Risk Grade A, to 14.25% for Risk Grade B, 17.00% for Risk Grade C, and 19.75% for Risk Grade D. Corporate lending is priced at ACRR plus a spread of 0.75% for Risk Grade A, 1.50% for Risk Grade B, and 2.75% for Risk Grade C.

Processing fees are 0.50% of sanctioned amount for home loans, subject to a minimum of AUR 5,000 and maximum of AUR 75,000; 1.75% of approved amount for personal loans, subject to a minimum of AUR 1,000 and maximum of AUR 25,000; and 1.00% of sanctioned limit for corporate facilities, subject to a cap of AUR 2,000,000.

Late payment fees across all lending products are 2% of the overdue installment amount per month of delay, subject to a minimum charge of AUR 250 per occurrence. Foreclosure charges differ by product: floating-rate home loans carry no foreclosure charge for individual borrowers; fixed-rate home loans carry a foreclosure charge of 2% of outstanding principal if repaid within the first 3 years, reducing to 1% thereafter; personal loans carry a foreclosure charge of 2% of outstanding principal if repaid within the first 12 months, and no charge thereafter.

Deposit interest is paid at 3.25% per annum on the Aurelia Savings Access Account and 3.75% per annum on the Preferred Current Account's linked savings sweep, calculated daily on closing balance and credited quarterly. Fixed deposits earn 7.50% per annum for a 1-year tenure, 7.75% for a 3-year tenure, and 8.00% for a 5-year tenure. Current accounts, other than the Preferred Current Account sweep balance, do not earn interest.

The Non-Maintenance Charge is AUR 500 per month for a Standard Savings account falling below the AUR 5,000 minimum average balance, and AUR 1,000 per month for a Preferred Current Account falling below the AUR 50,000 minimum average balance, both as defined in the Retail Banking Policy. ATM transactions at non-Aurelia Bank ATMs are free for the first 5 transactions in a calendar month, after which a fee of AUR 25 per transaction applies.

Aurelia Preferred Customers with a minimum relationship tenure of 3 years receive a permanent waiver of ATM fees at non-Aurelia Bank ATMs, regardless of transaction count. Fixed deposit rates are increased by 0.25% per annum for senior citizens aged 60 years or older across all tenures, as a standing product feature rather than a case-by-case exception.

Rate changes approved by Treasury are pushed to the core banking system through a scheduled quarterly batch update. Fee schedule changes require Product division sign-off and a minimum 30 calendar day advance notice to affected customers before taking effect, communicated through statement inserts and the digital banking channel described in the Digital Banking and Transaction Policy (AUR-DB-010).

The Treasury Rate Committee is responsible for setting and publishing ABLR and ACRR each quarter, based on prevailing funding costs and market benchmarks. The Product division is responsible for setting and revising service and transaction fees, subject to Finance division sign-off. Branch and digital channel staff are responsible for communicating current rates and fees accurately to customers but hold no authority to modify any rate or fee outside the exceptions explicitly defined in the relevant product manual.

For floating-rate loans, the applicable spread over ABLR, once assigned at origination based on the borrower's Risk Grade at that time, remains fixed for the life of the loan unless the borrower's Risk Grade is formally reassessed and a spread change is approved under the Credit Risk and Eligibility Policy (AUR-CR-008). Only the ABLR component resets quarterly; the Risk Grade-based spread is not automatically adjusted merely because ABLR has changed. Where a Risk Grade reassessment does result in a spread change, the revised rate takes effect from the borrower's next scheduled installment date, and the borrower is notified in writing at least 15 calendar days in advance.

Changes to ABLR and ACRR are approved by the Treasury Rate Committee. Changes to product spreads by Risk Grade require joint sign-off from the Treasury Rate Committee and the Central Credit Committee. Changes to service and transaction fees require Product division and Finance division sign-off, with fee increases above 20% of the existing fee requiring additional Senior Management approval.

This policy defines the Aurelia Credit Score methodology and the resulting Risk Grade classification used across all lending decisions at Aurelia Bank. It establishes the scoring inputs, grade boundaries, and portfolio monitoring standards that the Home Loan Product Manual (AUR-HL-002), Personal Loan Product Manual (AUR-PL-003), and Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004) rely upon when stating eligibility thresholds. Because every lending product references Risk Grade rather than restating its own scoring logic, this policy functions as shared infrastructure: a change made here propagates automatically to eligibility and pricing across the entire lending portfolio, which is why amendments require Board Credit Committee approval regardless of how narrow the change appears.

This policy applies to every credit application and every existing credit exposure held by Aurelia Bank, across retail, small business, and corporate segments. It is owned by the Credit Risk division and governs the work of credit analysts, the Regional Credit Committees, the Central Credit Committee, and the Board Credit Committee.

Aurelia Credit Score (ACS):: A proprietary score ranging from 300 to 900, calculated for every credit applicant and recalculated monthly for every existing borrower, used to derive a Risk Grade.

Risk Grade:: A letter classification from A to E derived from a customer's Aurelia Credit Score, used to determine loan eligibility, pricing spread, and required collateral across all lending products.

Special Mention Account (SMA):: An account classification applied when a borrower's installment or interest payment is between 30 and 89 days past due.

Non-Performing Exposure (NPE):: An account classification applied when a borrower's installment or interest payment is 90 days or more past due, triggering mandatory provisioning and restricted further lending.

Every applicant for credit at Aurelia Bank, regardless of product, must have an Aurelia Credit Score calculated prior to any lending decision. Individuals with no prior credit history are assigned a provisional score based on income, employment stability, and banking relationship tenure, capped at a maximum provisional Risk Grade of B until 12 months of repayment history is established on an active Aurelia Bank facility.

The Aurelia Credit Score is calculated from five weighted components: repayment history, weighted at 35%; credit utilization ratio across existing facilities, weighted at 30%; length of banking relationship, weighted at 15%; income or turnover stability, weighted at 10%; and total existing credit exposure relative to income, weighted at 10%. Each component is scored independently and combined to produce the final score, which is recalculated on the first business day of each month for every active borrower and on-demand at the point of any new application.

Risk Grades are assigned as follows: Risk Grade A corresponds to an Aurelia Credit Score of 750 or above; Risk Grade B corresponds to a score between 700 and 749; Risk Grade C corresponds to a score between 650 and 699; Risk Grade D corresponds to a score between 600 and 649; and Risk Grade E corresponds to a score below 600. Risk Grade E applicants are ineligible for Aurelia Personal Credit Line under any circumstance and are ineligible for Aurelia Home Advantage and corporate facilities except where explicitly permitted through the exception pathways defined in the respective product manuals.

Accounts with payments between 30 and 89 days past due are classified as Special Mention Accounts and carry a mandatory provisioning requirement of 1% of outstanding exposure. Accounts 90 days or more past due are classified as Non-Performing Exposures and are further sub-classified as Substandard, at 25% provisioning, for exposures 90 to 179 days past due; Doubtful, at 50% provisioning, for exposures 180 to 365 days past due; and Loss, at 100% provisioning, for exposures beyond 365 days past due.

An applicant with an Aurelia Credit Score below the standard threshold for a given product may be considered under the specific collateral or co-applicant exception pathways defined in the Home Loan Product Manual, Personal Loan Product Manual, or Corporate Loan Policy, but in every case such exceptions require approval at least one level above the standard approval authority for the facility size in question. No exception may result in lending to a Risk Grade E applicant for an unsecured product.

Aurelia Credit Score calculation is fully automated and runs as part of the core credit decisioning engine at the point of application, drawing on internal repayment history, declared income or turnover, and external credit bureau data where available. For new-to-bank applicants without internal repayment history, the provisional scoring methodology described above is applied. Monthly recalculation for existing borrowers runs as a batch process on the first business day of each month, and any resulting Risk Grade downgrade triggers an automated notification to the relevant Relationship Manager for portfolio follow-up.

Credit Risk Managers are responsible for reviewing and approving any manual override of a system-generated Aurelia Credit Score, and for maintaining the scoring model's component weightings. Relationship Managers are responsible for following up on Risk Grade downgrade notifications for their assigned portfolio, including initiating customer contact where a downgrade suggests emerging financial distress. The Central Credit Committee is responsible for quarterly portfolio-level review, and the Board Credit Committee is responsible for approving any change to the scoring methodology itself, including component weightings or Risk Grade boundaries.

Where a credit facility is secured, collateral is valued by an Aurelia Bank-empanelled valuer at origination and revalued periodically thereafter: property collateral securing Aurelia Home Advantage facilities is revalued every 3 years, while fixed asset collateral securing Aurelia Corporate Term Finance facilities is revalued annually, reflecting the comparatively higher volatility of business assets. A revaluation showing a decline in collateral value of more than 15% relative to the value used at origination triggers a mandatory review of the facility's LTV or security coverage, which may require the borrower to provide additional collateral or make a partial repayment to restore the required coverage ratio.

Aurelia Credit Score calculation itself does not require manual approval, as it is a systematic process governed by this policy. However, any manual override of a system-generated score, whether upward or downward, requires written justification and sign-off from a Credit Risk Manager. Portfolio-level Risk Grade distribution is reviewed quarterly by the Central Credit Committee, and any material deterioration in the overall portfolio's average Risk Grade is escalated to the Board Credit Committee.

This policy defines the Aurelia Credit Score, ranging from 300 to 900, and the five Risk Grades derived from it, from Grade A at 750 and above down to Grade E below 600. It sets the provisioning framework for Special Mention Accounts and Non-Performing Exposures, and establishes the eligibility floor of Risk Grade C or better used consistently across the Home Loan, Personal Loan, and Corporate Loan policies, subject only to the narrow, senior-approved exception pathways each product manual defines.

This document sets out Aurelia Bank's internal implementation of fictional regulatory obligations owed to the Aurelia Financial Regulatory Commission (AFRC) and the Aurelia National Deposit Insurance Corporation (ANDIC), the two fictional supervisory bodies referenced throughout this synthetic corpus. It defines capital and liquidity requirements, regulatory reporting obligations, record retention standards, and restricted business sectors, and provides the compliance basis referenced by the Corporate Loan Policy (AUR-CL-004) and the KYC and AML Policy (AUR-KYC-006). All figures, bodies, and requirements described in this document are fictional and constructed solely for research purposes; they do not describe any real regulator or regulation. Every other policy in this corpus that imposes a retention period, a reporting deadline, or a sector exclusion ultimately traces that requirement back to this document.

This regulation applies to Aurelia Bank as a whole, including all business divisions, branches, and digital channels. It governs prudential ratios calculated at the whole-bank level, as well as reporting, retention, and sector-restriction obligations that apply to individual customer relationships and transactions across the retail and corporate segments.

Aurelia Financial Regulatory Commission (AFRC):: The fictional national supervisory authority to which Aurelia Bank submits regulatory filings under this synthetic framework.

Aurelia National Deposit Insurance Corporation (ANDIC):: The fictional deposit insurance body providing coverage to Aurelia Bank depositors under this synthetic framework.

Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):: The ratio of Aurelia Bank's regulatory capital to its risk-weighted assets, expressed as a percentage.

Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR):: The ratio of Aurelia Bank's high-quality liquid assets to its projected net cash outflows over a 30-day stress period.

Aurelia Statutory Reserve Ratio (ASRR):: The proportion of eligible deposits that Aurelia Bank must hold with AFRC in reserve form, rather than deploy into lending or investment.

Restricted Sector:: A category of business activity in which Aurelia Bank does not extend credit, as defined under this regulation.

This regulation applies uniformly to Aurelia Bank; there is no customer-level eligibility criterion for the prudential ratio requirements. Sector restrictions defined below apply to the eligibility of Corporate Customers and Small Business Customers for any lending product, as cross-referenced in the Corporate Loan Policy.

Aurelia Bank is required to maintain a minimum Capital Adequacy Ratio of 11.5% at all times, calculated at the end of each business day and formally reported to AFRC quarterly. Aurelia Bank is required to maintain a minimum Liquidity Coverage Ratio of 100%, monitored daily by the Treasury division. Aurelia Bank is required to hold an Aurelia Statutory Reserve Ratio of 4.5% of eligible customer deposits with AFRC, calculated on a fortnightly average basis.

Depositor funds are insured by ANDIC up to a maximum of AUR 500,000 per depositor, per institution, across all deposit accounts held in that depositor's name. This insurance limit applies automatically and does not require a separate application by the customer.

Quarterly regulatory filings, including the Capital Adequacy Report and Liquidity Position Report, are due to AFRC within 21 calendar days of each quarter end. Any breach of the minimum Capital Adequacy Ratio or Liquidity Coverage Ratio must be reported to AFRC within 2 business days of the breach being identified, together with a remediation plan.

Restricted Sectors, in which Aurelia Bank does not extend credit under the Corporate Loan Policy or any other lending product, include unlicensed gaming operations, entities under active AFRC sanction, and any business appearing on the Financial Intelligence Unit-Aurelia watchlist referenced in the KYC and AML Policy. Applications from entities in adjacent but non-restricted sectors, such as licensed hospitality with an incidental gaming license, require additional Senior Credit Committee review even though they are not automatically excluded.

Customer records, including KYC documentation, transaction history, and account statements, must be retained for a minimum of 8 years following account closure. Suspicious Transaction Report and Cash Transaction Report filings, together with their supporting documentation, must be retained for a minimum of 10 years from the date of filing.

A temporary Capital Adequacy Ratio shortfall arising from a one-off event, such as a large impairment recognized in a single reporting period, may be reported to AFRC with a remediation plan extending up to 2 quarters, subject to Board approval, without triggering the standard 2 business day breach notification if the shortfall is identified and disclosed proactively within the same reporting cycle in which it arose. No exception is available to the Restricted Sector exclusion; sector restrictions may only be lifted through formal policy amendment approved by the Board Credit Committee.

Daily Capital Adequacy Ratio and Liquidity Coverage Ratio calculations are performed automatically by the Treasury Risk system and reviewed each morning by the Treasury Risk team. Quarterly regulatory filings are compiled by the Regulatory Reporting team, reviewed by the Chief Financial Officer, and submitted to AFRC through the designated regulatory filing portal. Record retention is managed through the bank's document management system, which automatically flags records for review at the 8-year and 10-year retention milestones described above, rather than deleting them automatically, pending a manual disposal review.

The Chief Financial Officer is accountable for the accuracy and timely submission of all quarterly regulatory filings to AFRC. The Treasury Risk team is responsible for daily monitoring of the Capital Adequacy Ratio and Liquidity Coverage Ratio and for escalating any threshold breach within the 2 business day window described above. The Compliance division is responsible for maintaining the Restricted Sector list, for approving record disposal following the retention review milestone, and for coordinating Aurelia Bank's response to any AFRC examination.

Aurelia Bank commissions an independent annual compliance audit, covering adherence to the Capital Adequacy Ratio, Liquidity Coverage Ratio, and Aurelia Statutory Reserve Ratio requirements, the accuracy of quarterly AFRC filings, and the effectiveness of the Restricted Sector exclusion process described in the Corporate Loan Policy. Findings are presented to the Board Credit Committee within 45 calendar days of audit completion, and any finding classified as a material weakness requires a remediation plan with defined milestones, tracked by the Compliance division until closure.

Quarterly regulatory filings require Chief Financial Officer sign-off prior to submission. Any Restricted Sector exception request, though generally unavailable, must in all cases be escalated to and decided by the Board Credit Committee. Record disposal following the retention review milestone requires Compliance division sign-off before any record is permanently deleted.

Aurelia Bank maintains an internal whistleblower channel through which any employee may report a suspected breach of this regulation, including a suspected Restricted Sector violation or a suspected Capital Adequacy Ratio misstatement, directly to the Compliance division without going through their line management. Reports may be submitted anonymously, and the Compliance division is required to acknowledge receipt within 3 business days and to provide a substantive response or investigation update within 30 calendar days. Retaliation against an employee for a good-faith report made through this channel is treated as a disciplinary matter independent of the underlying report's outcome.
